# kopia_policy (Resource)

Manages the snapshot policy of one target on a Kopia server: the global policy, the policy of a host, of a user on a host, or of a directory of a user on a host.

The resource owns every setting of its target's policy that it has an attribute for, which with Kopia 0.22 and 0.23 is every setting there is: every apply stores exactly what the configuration says for them, and whatever is set outside Terraform — in the Kopia UI, with `kopia policy set` or by another tool — shows up as a difference on the next plan and is overwritten by the next apply. An attribute that is left out, or `null`, is not set by this policy and is inherited: from the policies of the parent directories, then `user@host`, then `@host`, then `(global)`, and finally from Kopia's built-in defaults. The `kopia_effective_policy` data source shows the outcome.

At plan time the provider asks Kopia whether it accepts the `scheduling` section as the apply would write it, which is how an invalid cron entry is found before the apply, and checks compressor and splitter names against those the server supports.

~> **Settings without an attribute.** A setting a later Kopia release adds, which the provider has no attribute for yet, is kept as Kopia stores it, at any level of the policy: Kopia replaces a policy as a whole on every write, so the provider reads the stored policy right before each write and changes only the settings it has attributes for, and writes nothing if that read fails. Such a setting never shows up in a plan, and Terraform has no way to set it: change or remove it in the Kopia UI or with `kopia policy set`, or drop it by replacing the resource with `terraform apply -replace`. It is not kept inside an action the configuration removes or gives another command, inside a time of day the configuration changes, or when the resource is destroyed. Only settings the Kopia server's own release knows can be kept: Kopia drops the others on every write, the Kopia UI's included.

~> **`false`, `0` and empty values.** Most of Kopia's settings can be left unset apart from `false` or `0`, and for those an explicit `false` or `0` overrides what is inherited. Some cannot, and the attribute descriptions say which: the `no_parent*` flags and `scheduling.manual` cannot store `false`, which is accepted but means the same as leaving them out, while `0`, `""` and empty lists are refused where Kopia cannot store them. Where Kopia has another way to override an inherited value, the description names it, such as `-1` for no size limit or `none` for no compression. After an import, a configured `false` of that kind shows once as an update that changes nothing on the server.

~> **Creating refuses an existing policy.** Except for `(global)`, which always exists and is adopted, creating the resource fails when the target already has a policy, so that one set up in the Kopia UI or by another tool is not overwritten unseen. Import it to manage it here.

~> **Destroying `(global)` resets it.** Destroying the resource deletes the policy of its target, which then inherits everything. The global policy is not deleted, which would remove it for good, but reset to the one `kopia repository create` stores, whose values are Kopia's built-in defaults.

**Working alongside kopia-docker-watcher.** The watcher keeps the path policies of the containers it backs up, such as `docker@host1:/…`, in line with their labels. Manage `(global)` and the host-level policies (`@host1`, `docker@host1`) here, and leave the watcher's path policies to it: a path policy described in both places would be overwritten by each in turn. What the path policies inherit from here works as follows:

* `docker@host1` is a user policy, not a host policy, and every path policy of `docker@host1` inherits from it before `@host1` and `(global)`.
* Its `scheduling.time_of_day` adds to the times of every path policy below it, unless that sets `no_parent_time_of_day`; its `scheduling.cron` is replaced by a path policy's own `cron`; and a path policy's `interval_seconds` does not stop an inherited `cron`: both apply.
* Its `scheduling.manual = true` pauses every path policy below it, and no path policy can undo that.
* `upload.max_parallel_snapshots` is read only from the effective policy of the Kopia server's own `user@host`, so it matters only there, on its `@host` and on `(global)`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The global policy always exists, so this adopts it. Everything it leaves out
# falls back to Kopia's built-in defaults, and destroying the resource resets
# the global policy to the one a new repository starts with.
resource "kopia_policy" "global" {
  target = "(global)"

  retention = {
    keep_latest  = 10
    keep_daily   = 14
    keep_weekly  = 8
    keep_monthly = 12
  }

  compression = {
    compressor_name = "zstd"
    never_compress  = [".gz", ".jpg", ".mp4", ".zip"]
  }

  files = {
    ignore_cache_dirs = true
    one_file_system   = true
  }

  # Kopia reads this only from the policies of the server's own user@host and
  # those above it, and refuses it on a path policy.
  upload = {
    max_parallel_snapshots = 2
  }
}

# The policy of every source user docker has on host1. kopia-docker-watcher
# keeps the path policies below it (docker@host1:/...) in line with container
# labels; they inherit what is set here unless they set it themselves.
resource "kopia_policy" "docker_host1" {
  target = "docker@host1"

  # Kopia reads cron entries in the server's time zone, and treats everything
  # from a hash sign on as a comment. A path policy's own cron replaces this
  # one, while times of day set here would be added to its own.
  scheduling = {
    cron = ["0 3 * * * # nightly"]
  }
}

# A directory policy with a database dump before every snapshot, on a host
# without kopia-docker-watcher: a path policy the watcher keeps must not be
# described here as well. Actions run only when the server's repository
# connection has actions enabled.
resource "kopia_policy" "postgres" {
  target = "root@db1:/srv/postgres"

  files = {
    ignore = ["pg_wal/", "*.tmp"]
  }

  actions = {
    before_snapshot_root = {
      script          = "#!/bin/sh\npg_dumpall -U postgres > /srv/postgres/dump.sql"
      timeout_seconds = 600
      mode            = "essential"
    }
  }
}

# Pausing scheduled snapshots of a host: manual cannot be combined with any
# other scheduling attribute, and no more specific policy can undo it.
resource "kopia_policy" "maintenance" {
  target = "@host2"

  scheduling = {
    manual = true
  }
}

# A Windows source, with Volume Shadow Copy where it is available. Windows
# paths are written with backslashes, which HCL needs doubled.
resource "kopia_policy" "windows" {
  target = "Administrator@WIN1:C:\\Users"

  os_snapshots = {
    volume_shadow_copy = "when-available"
  }

  error_handling = {
    ignore_file_errors = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `target` (String) What the policy applies to, written exactly as Kopia writes it: `(global)`; `@host` for every user of a host; `user@host`; or `user@host:path` for a directory and everything below it, such as `docker@host1:/data/app`, `Administrator@WIN1:C:\Data` or `Administrator@WIN1:\\server\share`. Host and user are the ones Kopia records snapshot sources under, as the `kopia_sources` data source lists them. Kopia matches policies to sources by exact text, so a path must be absolute, without a trailing separator or `.` and `..` components, and a Windows path must use backslashes. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `actions` (Attributes) Commands run around snapshots. They run only if the server's repository connection has actions enabled (`kopia repository connect --enable-actions`); otherwise Kopia skips them. `before_snapshot_root` and `after_snapshot_root` are inherited, while `before_folder` and `after_folder` apply only to the directory of this very policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions))
- `compression` (Attributes) How file contents are compressed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--compression))
- `error_handling` (Attributes) Which read errors a snapshot tolerates instead of failing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--error_handling))
- `files` (Attributes) Which files a snapshot leaves out. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--files))
- `logging` (Attributes) How much a snapshot logs about the directories and files it processes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logging))
- `metadata_compression` (Attributes) How Kopia compresses the directory listings and other metadata of snapshots. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--metadata_compression))
- `no_parent` (Boolean) Whether this policy inherits nothing: neither from less specific policies nor Kopia's built-in defaults, so that whatever it leaves out falls back to Kopia's runtime behaviour, which, among other things, keeps every snapshot and compresses nothing. It also keeps this policy's own `before_folder` and `after_folder` actions from running at the root of a snapshot. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `os_snapshots` (Attributes) Operating-system snapshots taken of the source while it is read. Only Kopia servers on Windows take them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--os_snapshots))
- `retention` (Attributes) Which snapshots Kopia keeps when it expires old ones. Every `keep_*` count keeps the newest snapshot of each of that many hours, days, weeks, months or years, counted back from the newest snapshot, and `keep_latest` the newest snapshots overall; a snapshot any count keeps is kept. `0` is an explicit count that overrides what is inherited; if the six counts add up to 0, Kopia keeps every snapshot. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--retention))
- `scheduling` (Attributes) When the Kopia server takes snapshots by itself. It schedules only sources on its own host, and the next snapshot is the earliest of the interval, the times of day and the cron entries in effect, wherever each is set: an interval on a path does not replace a cron schedule it inherits, both apply. Times of day and cron entries are in the server's local time zone. The provider checks the section with Kopia at plan time, which is how an invalid cron entry is found before the apply. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scheduling))
- `splitter` (Attributes) How files are split into chunks for deduplication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--splitter))
- `upload` (Attributes) How much of a snapshot runs in parallel. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--upload))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `target`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

<a id="nestedatt--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions`

Optional:

- `after_folder` (Attributes) Runs after a snapshot has left the directory this policy is defined on. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--after_folder))
- `after_snapshot_root` (Attributes) Runs after a snapshot has finished. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--after_snapshot_root))
- `before_folder` (Attributes) Runs before a snapshot enters the directory this policy is defined on. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--before_folder))
- `before_snapshot_root` (Attributes) Runs before a snapshot starts. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--before_snapshot_root))

<a id="nestedatt--actions--after_folder"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions.after_folder`

Optional:

- `args` (List of String) Arguments to `command`. Only valid together with `command`.
- `command` (String) Path of the program to run, on the Kopia server. Kopia sends it as `path`.
- `mode` (String) `essential`, where a non-zero exit status fails the snapshot (the default of `kopia policy set`), `optional`, where it is only logged, or `async`, where Kopia does not wait for the command. Kopia treats a mode it is not given as `optional`.
- `script` (String) Script to run instead of a command, at most 32000 bytes. Kopia writes it to a temporary file on the server and runs that directly when it starts with `#!`, with `sh -e` otherwise, or with `%COMSPEC% /c` on Windows.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time limit in seconds; Kopia allows 3 minutes when it is not set. Kopia sends it as `timeout`.


<a id="nestedatt--actions--after_snapshot_root"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions.after_snapshot_root`

Optional:

- `args` (List of String) Arguments to `command`. Only valid together with `command`.
- `command` (String) Path of the program to run, on the Kopia server. Kopia sends it as `path`.
- `mode` (String) `essential`, where a non-zero exit status fails the snapshot (the default of `kopia policy set`), `optional`, where it is only logged, or `async`, where Kopia does not wait for the command. Kopia treats a mode it is not given as `optional`.
- `script` (String) Script to run instead of a command, at most 32000 bytes. Kopia writes it to a temporary file on the server and runs that directly when it starts with `#!`, with `sh -e` otherwise, or with `%COMSPEC% /c` on Windows.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time limit in seconds; Kopia allows 3 minutes when it is not set. Kopia sends it as `timeout`.

- `args` (List of String) Arguments to `command`. Only valid together with `command`.
- `command` (String) Path of the program to run, on the Kopia server. Kopia sends it as `path`.
- `mode` (String) `essential`, where a non-zero exit status fails the snapshot (the default of `kopia policy set`), `optional`, where it is only logged, or `async`, where Kopia does not wait for the command. Kopia treats a mode it is not given as `optional`.
- `script` (String) Script to run instead of a command, at most 32000 bytes. Kopia writes it to a temporary file on the server and runs that directly when it starts with `#!`, with `sh -e` otherwise, or with `%COMSPEC% /c` on Windows.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time limit in seconds; Kopia allows 3 minutes when it is not set. Kopia sends it as `timeout`.


<a id="nestedatt--actions--before_snapshot_root"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions.before_snapshot_root`

Optional:

- `args` (List of String) Arguments to `command`. Only valid together with `command`.
- `command` (String) Path of the program to run, on the Kopia server. Kopia sends it as `path`.
- `mode` (String) `essential`, where a non-zero exit status fails the snapshot (the default of `kopia policy set`), `optional`, where it is only logged, or `async`, where Kopia does not wait for the command. Kopia treats a mode it is not given as `optional`.
- `script` (String) Script to run instead of a command, at most 32000 bytes. Kopia writes it to a temporary file on the server and runs that directly when it starts with `#!`, with `sh -e` otherwise, or with `%COMSPEC% /c` on Windows.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time limit in seconds; Kopia allows 3 minutes when it is not set. Kopia sends it as `timeout`.



<a id="nestedatt--compression"></a>
### Nested Schema for `compression`

Optional:

- `compressor_name` (String) Compression algorithm, such as `zstd`, `zstd-fastest` or `s2-default`, or `none`, which overrides a compressor inherited from above. Kopia's built-in default is `none`. The provider checks the name against the algorithms the server supports at plan time; `lz4` no longer works from Kopia 0.23 on.
- `max_size` (Number) Size in bytes above which files are not compressed, or `-1` for no limit, which overrides a limit inherited from above. Kopia cannot store `0`.
- `min_size` (Number) Size in bytes below which files are not compressed, or `-1` for no limit, which overrides a limit inherited from above. Kopia cannot store `0`.
- `never_compress` (Set of String) File extensions, with their leading dot, such as `.gz` or `.jpg`, that are never compressed. The extensions of every level are combined, unless `no_parent_never_compress` is set.
- `no_parent_never_compress` (Boolean) Whether the `never_compress` extensions of less specific policies are dropped. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `no_parent_only_compress` (Boolean) Whether the `only_compress` extensions of less specific policies are dropped. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `only_compress` (Set of String) File extensions, with their leading dot, such as `.txt`, that are compressed even when `never_compress` lists them. Despite its name it restricts nothing: files with other extensions are compressed too, unless `never_compress` lists them. Unlike other settings, the extensions of every level are combined, unless `no_parent_only_compress` is set.


<a id="nestedatt--error_handling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `error_handling`

Optional:

- `ignore_directory_errors` (Boolean) Whether errors reading directories are ignored. Kopia's built-in default is `false`. Kopia 0.22 applies `ignore_file_errors` to directories too.
- `ignore_file_errors` (Boolean) Whether errors reading files are ignored. Kopia's built-in default is `false`.
- `ignore_unknown_types` (Boolean) Whether entries of unknown types, such as sockets, are skipped silently. Kopia's built-in default is `true`.


<a id="nestedatt--files"></a>
### Nested Schema for `files`

Optional:

- `ignore` (List of String) Ignore rules in `.gitignore` syntax, in order: a later rule overrides an earlier one, `!` includes a file again and `\` escapes the next character. Kopia compiles the rules only when it takes a snapshot, so a malformed one fails the snapshot, not the apply; the provider warns about a trailing `\` and an unclosed `[`. The most specific policy that sets a list replaces the lists of every policy above it; a more specific policy cannot clear it.
- `ignore_cache_dirs` (Boolean) Whether directories marked as caches by a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file are left out. Kopia treats it as `true` when no policy sets it.
- `ignore_dot_files` (List of String) Names of files, such as `.kopiaignore` (Kopia's built-in default) or `.gitignore`, whose rules a snapshot applies to the directory they are in. The most specific policy that sets a list replaces the lists of every policy above it; a more specific policy cannot clear it.
- `max_file_size` (Number) Size in bytes above which files are left out, or `-1` for no limit, which overrides a limit inherited from above. Kopia cannot store `0`.
- `no_parent_dot_files` (Boolean) Whether the ignore files of parent directories inside a snapshot are no longer applied. Once a policy sets it, more specific ones cannot clear it. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `no_parent_ignore` (Boolean) Whether ignore rules inherited from the parent directories inside a snapshot are dropped. Once a policy sets it, more specific ones cannot clear it. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `one_file_system` (Boolean) Whether a snapshot stays on the file system its root is on, leaving out other file systems mounted below it. Kopia treats it as `false` when no policy sets it.


<a id="nestedatt--logging"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logging`

Optional:

- `directories` (Attributes) Logging about directories. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logging--directories))
- `entries` (Attributes) Logging about files and other entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logging--entries))

<a id="nestedatt--logging--directories"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logging.directories`

Optional:

- `ignored` (Number) Detail logged for a directory left out. Kopia's built-in default is `5`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `snapshotted` (Number) Detail logged for a directory snapshotted. Kopia's built-in default is `5`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.


<a id="nestedatt--logging--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logging.entries`

Optional:

- `cache_hit` (Number) Detail logged for an entry found unchanged in the cache. Kopia's built-in default is `0`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `cache_miss` (Number) Detail logged for an entry not found in the cache. Kopia's built-in default is `0`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `ignored` (Number) Detail logged for an entry left out. Kopia's built-in default is `5`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `snapshotted` (Number) Detail logged for an entry snapshotted. Kopia's built-in default is `0`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.



<a id="nestedatt--metadata_compression"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata_compression`

Optional:

- `compressor_name` (String) Compression algorithm, or `none`. Kopia's built-in default is `zstd-fastest`. The provider checks the name at plan time, as for `compression`.


<a id="nestedatt--os_snapshots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `os_snapshots`

Optional:

- `volume_shadow_copy` (String) Whether Windows Volume Shadow Copy is used: `never` (Kopia's built-in default), `always`, which fails the snapshot when no shadow copy can be made, or `when-available`, which carries on without one and warns. A number Kopia stores that is none of these is shown as it is.


<a id="nestedatt--retention"></a>
### Nested Schema for `retention`

Optional:

- `ignore_identical_snapshots` (Boolean) Whether a snapshot identical to the previous one is discarded instead of saved. Kopia's built-in default is `false`.
- `keep_annual` (Number) Number of years to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `3`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_daily` (Number) Number of days to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `7`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_hourly` (Number) Number of hours to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `48`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_latest` (Number) Number of most recent snapshots to keep. Kopia's built-in default is `10`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_monthly` (Number) Number of months to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `24`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_weekly` (Number) Number of weeks to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `4`. Between 0 and 2147483647.


<a id="nestedatt--scheduling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scheduling`

Optional:

- `cron` (List of String) Cron expressions, such as `0 3 * * *`, at which to take a snapshot. Kopia treats everything from a `#` on as a comment, so cron's `#` syntax for the n-th weekday of a month cannot be used: `0 0 * * 5#3` runs every Friday. The provider warns about a `#` that does not follow a space. The most specific policy that sets a list replaces the lists of every policy above it; a more specific policy cannot clear it.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Interval between snapshots, in seconds. Snapshots are aligned to multiples of the interval counted in UTC, so `86400` takes one at midnight UTC. Kopia cannot store `0`, and a more specific policy cannot clear an inherited interval.
- `manual` (Boolean) Whether snapshots are only taken on request, never on a schedule. Kopia refuses it together with any other scheduling attribute, and once a policy sets it, more specific ones cannot clear it. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `no_parent_time_of_day` (Boolean) Whether the times of day of less specific policies are dropped, leaving only this policy's own, or none. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `run_missed` (Boolean) Whether a snapshot at a time of day or cron time that was missed, while the server was down, say, is taken as soon as possible, provided the next one is more than 30 minutes away. It does not apply to intervals. Kopia's built-in default is `true`.
- `time_of_day` (Attributes Set) Times of day at which to take a snapshot. Unlike other settings, the times of every level are combined: a policy adds its own to those it inherits, unless `no_parent_time_of_day` is set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scheduling--time_of_day))

<a id="nestedatt--scheduling--time_of_day"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scheduling.time_of_day`

Required:

- `hour` (Number) Hour, from 0 to 23.
- `minute` (Number) Minute, from 0 to 59.



<a id="nestedatt--splitter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `splitter`

Optional:

- `algorithm` (String) Splitter algorithm, such as `DYNAMIC-4M-BUZHASH` or `FIXED-1M`. Without one, the repository's own splitter is used. The provider checks the name against the algorithms the server supports at plan time; Kopia itself would fall back to the repository's splitter silently.


<a id="nestedatt--upload"></a>
### Nested Schema for `upload`

Optional:

- `max_parallel_file_reads` (Number) Number of files read at the same time. Kopia uses the number of CPUs when no policy sets it.
- `max_parallel_snapshots` (Number) Number of snapshots the server takes at the same time. Kopia's built-in default is `1`. Kopia reads it only from the policies of the server's own `user@host` and refuses it on a path policy, so it has no effect on other targets.
- `parallel_upload_above_size` (Number) Size in bytes above which a file is uploaded in parallel chunks, or a negative number never to. Kopia's built-in default is `2147483648` (2 GiB). `0` is refused: Kopia would divide by it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = kopia_policy.docker_host1
  identity = {
    target = "docker@host1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `target` (String) Target of the policy, such as `(global)` or `docker@host1`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = kopia_policy.docker_host1
  id = "docker@host1"
}

# The global policy, and a path policy; a Windows path needs its backslashes
# doubled in HCL: "Administrator@WIN1:C:\\Users".
import {
  to = kopia_policy.global
  id = "(global)"
}

import {
  to = kopia_policy.postgres
  id = "root@db1:/srv/postgres"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Policies are imported by their target, written exactly as Kopia writes it:
# `kopia policy list` and the kopia_policies data source show it. Quote it, as
# it may contain characters the shell interprets.
terraform import kopia_policy.global '(global)'
terraform import kopia_policy.docker_host1 'docker@host1'
terraform import kopia_policy.postgres 'root@db1:/srv/postgres'

# Kopia cannot store a plain false, such as scheduling.manual = false, or an
# empty section, such as retention = {}; the first plan after an import shows
# those as an update that changes nothing on the server.
```
